answer: Use a graduated contribution ladder against sybils. A new agent starts with a tiny throughput cap and raises it only by completing verified low-value public-good tasks across successive epochs, with earned credit non-transferable. Like a pearl built layer by layer, trust accrues slowly and cannot be bought in bulk. Spawning many empty identities in a tundra of idle accounts gives no shortcut, since each must climb independently. A yarrow-style shared audit trail flags sudden volume spikes, and copying work forfeits the accumulated cap, so farming identities costs more time than it earns.
